function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

• Youth tournaments, national team camps, and exhibition games often take place in the capital. | | **Convenient transport & lodging** – most international flights land at Keflavík Airport, just ~45 min drive away. Hotels range from boutique guesthouses to luxury chains, many offering easy access to the rinks. | • Public transit links the airport, downtown, and the sports complex.
• Restaurants, cafés, museums, and nightlife keep visitors entertained after the game. | | **Cultural depth + winter fun** – beyond hockey you can explore Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa Concert Hall, the Golden Circle, geothermal spas, and even catch a midnight sun stroll along the harbor. | • A full day itinerary fits around a match schedule without feeling rushed. | --- ### How to make the most of your trip 1. **Book tickets early** - Check the official websites of HK Grótta and ÍBÍ for season schedules. - Some clubs sell tickets through third‑party platforms—look for verified sellers to avoid scams. 2. **Plan a “game day” route** - Arrive at least 30–60 minutes before kickoff to soak in pre‑match atmosphere. - Many clubs offer fan zones where you can try local snacks, buy merchandise, and sometimes get autographs. 3. **Combine sport with sightseeing** - After the game, head back into town for dinner at a traditional Icelandic restaurant (try lamb soup or fermented shark!). - In the evening, consider a short walk across the bridge over the Lagarfljót river or a quick dip in the Blue Lagoon (if you’re willing to stretch the day). --- ## Alternative: Akúreyri (“Akureyri”) – the second‑tier hotspot If you prefer a quieter setting but still want solid hockey vibes: | Feature | Details | |---------|--------| | **Home of Skautafélagið Fram** | One of Iceland’s oldest clubs, playing at the *Skautahúsin* arena. | | **Smaller crowds, intimate feel** | Games attract locals and regional supporters—a great way to see community spirit firsthand. | | **Northern charm** | Surrounded by fjords and mountains; perfect for hiking, whale watching, and exploring the Arctic landscape. | | **Accessibility** | Flights connect via Reykjavík; trains run daily between the two capitals (~5 hours). | While Reykjavík offers the breadth of experience, Akúreyri gives you a taste of Icelandic life outside the capital while still enjoying competitive hockey. --- ### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Do I need a special visa?** | Most travelers enter under the Schengen Visa Waiver Program.
